headline: Stocks slip as oil, Canada tariffs, and rate-hike odds collide
body: US futures opened the week softer, with Dow contracts down roughly 0.6-0.7% and the S&P and Nasdaq off more modestly, as three pressures stacked up at once. Crude extended its climb — WTI near $92 and Brent above $97 — after Iran threatened retaliation following US strikes on its oil tankers near Kharg Island, reviving a geopolitical risk premium tied to the Strait of Hormuz; Goldman raised its year-end Brent/WTI forecasts on the assumption that Gulf shipping disruption persists into 2027. Canada's retaliatory tariffs of 15-50% on roughly $27.6 billion of US goods took effect today, layering fresh trade friction onto steel, aluminum, appliances, and agricultural equipment. Underneath both, Friday's much-hotter-than-expected August payrolls print (162,000 versus a roughly 53,000 estimate) pushed CME-implied odds of a Fed rate hike this month to about 58%, with the 2-year Treasury yield at its highest since January 2025. Friday's CPI print is now the week's pivotal data point.

Sentiment trackers have drifted toward Fear (a widely cited third-party gauge put it around 42 today), a cooler tone than the more complacent, low-put-buying readings seen in prior sessions — consistent with a market pricing geopolitical and rate risk rather than panicking outright. Retail chatter on Reddit and WallStreetBets stayed concentrated in mega-cap AI names — Nvidia, Alphabet, and Apple — still discussed bullishly even as the broader tape softened, alongside a sharp jump in Nike mentions; beyond that concentration there wasn't much distinct social-sentiment signal today, so this read leans more on price action and headlines than on retail positioning. Taken together, the setup looks like headline-driven caution rather than fundamental deterioration, with oil, the Canada tariff rollout, and rate-hike odds as the swing factors into Friday's CPI.
